## SC-SCA-POSS-001: StarCraft abilities: possession and deliverance

Request: Shax t587u (2026-11-25). Catalogue: docs/STARCRAFT_ABILITY_THEOLOGY_MAP.md. Evidence: docs/evidence/starcraft-abilities/abilities.jsonl.

### Invariant
Control is separable from the host. A possessor can take a host's actuators without consuming the host. Liberation is a distinct operation from healing, and it acts on the controller, the binding or the channel, not on the host.

Texts: Mark 5:1-15; Mark 9:17-27; Matt 12:29; Mark 1:34; Luke 9:1; Matt 10:8; Luke 13:11-16

SC-MAFUBA-001 clauses illustrated: 001A. Illustration only; SC-MAFUBA-001 is Proposed GOLD, gold_awarded false, not validated by this entry.

### STRONG rows

#### SC2-Z13 — Infestor: Neural Parasite [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Channelled: the Infestor takes control of one enemy unit through a visible tether. It ends if the Infestor is killed, the player cancels, or the victim is moved more than 14 range away. The Infestor cannot act while channelling. Heroic units cannot be targeted. The victim returns to its owner intact.
- Counterpart (text): Possession in the Gospels: a spirit drives the host's body against the host; the man is returned 'clothed and in his right mind'; liberation acts on the possessor (the strong man is bound), not on the host.
- Citation: Mark 5:1-15; Mark 9:17-27; Matt 12:29
- Invariant (interpretation): Control is separable from the host. The possessor takes the actuators without consuming the host, and liberation acts on the controller or its channel, not by destroying the host.
- Residual: Neural Parasite lasts seconds and is a tactic; Gospel possession lasts years. The Infestor is vulnerable while it controls; the texts say nothing about a possessor's own vulnerability. Expulsion in the Gospels is by authority (a command), while the game breaks control by force or distance.
- MAFUBA: 001A: the canonical isolation failure. An adversary gains write access to the actuator fibre (orders) without touching protected state (the unit's HP and identity). Because state was never written, release is clean. Isolation must cover actuators, not only stored state.
- Sources: sc2/Infestor (Legacy of the Void)

#### BW-T03 — Medic: Restoration [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): A separate spell from Heal. Removes Lockdown, Optical Flare, Irradiate, Plague, Ensnare, Parasite and Maelstrom from one unit. It does not restore HP.
- Counterpart (text): Jesus heals the sick and casts out demons as two named acts; the Twelve receive authority over demons and to cure diseases; the woman 'whom Satan bound' is loosed.
- Citation: Mark 1:34; Luke 9:1; Matt 10:8; Luke 13:11-16
- Invariant (interpretation): Deliverance is a different operation from healing. Removing a hostile attachment or binding is not restoring damage, and the healer class carries both as distinct powers.
- Residual: Restoration also clears ordinary debuffs (Optical Flare, Ensnare), which are not 'spirits'. Luke 13 joins the two acts (the woman is loosed and her body straightened), while the game keeps them strictly apart. The distinction is the mapping; the texts make it often, not always.
- MAFUBA: 001A: removing an attachment (Parasite gives the enemy vision through the host) is an isolation repair, distinct from repairing state.
- Sources: bw/Medic

### Context rows (not STRONG; not promoted)

#### BW-P05 — Dark Archon: Mind Control [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Permanently and irreversibly transfers an enemy unit to the caster; the Dark Archon loses all its shields.
- Counterpart (text): Possession (Mark 5), but permanent; closer to a change of allegiance.
- Citation: Mark 5:1-15; Rom 6:16
- Invariant (interpretation): Control transferred at a cost to the controller.
- Residual: Gospel possession is not ownership transfer and is ended by deliverance; Mind Control is permanent. Romans 6:16 (slaves of the one you obey) is closer to allegiance than possession. The cost paid by the caster has no counterpart.
- MAFUBA: 001A: irreversible capture of the actuator fibre (worse than SC2-Z13: nothing to release).
- Sources: bw/Dark Archon

#### BW-Z02 — Queen: Parasite [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Attaches to an enemy unit; the Zerg player sees through it for the rest of the game. Only Restoration removes it.
- Counterpart (text): Satan entered into Judas; the one who shared bread lifted his heel.
- Citation: Luke 22:3; John 13:18, 13:27
- Invariant (interpretation): A hostile attachment that gives the adversary access through a member of the group.
- Residual: Judas acts; the parasited unit only carries the enemy's eye. The attachment-and-removal structure is graded with BW-T03 in the possession and deliverance cluster.
- MAFUBA: 001A: an exfiltration channel attached to a trusted node.
- Sources: bw/Queen (Unit)

#### BW-Z01 — Queen: Infest Command Center [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): A Terran Command Center damaged below half HP can be infested; it then belongs to the Zerg and produces Infested Terrans.
- Counterpart (text): Give no foothold (topos) to the devil; the empty house reoccupied.
- Citation: Eph 4:27; Matt 12:43-45
- Invariant (interpretation): A damaged structure becomes the enemy's foothold and is turned to produce for him.
- Residual: The breach condition (below half HP) fits 'foothold'. Matthew 12 is about an empty house, not a damaged one. Possession of a building that then produces weapons has no direct text.
- Sources: bw/Queen (Unit), bw/Infested Command Center

#### CMP-01 — Amon (LotV campaign): Corruption of the Khala [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Amon corrupts the Khala, the Protoss communal psychic link, and takes the Khalai connected to it under his thrall.
- Counterpart (text): The prince of the power of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience; you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons.
- Citation: Eph 2:2; 1 Cor 10:20-21
- Invariant (interpretation): Possession through a shared communion channel: whoever is on the channel is reachable.
- Residual: The structural point (a shared medium is an influence path) is explicit in the game and only implied in Ephesians 2:2. 1 Corinthians 10 forbids double communion; it does not describe takeover through it.
- MAFUBA: 001A / 001C: a shared bus is an influence path. Isolation must be per node, because a compromise of the shared channel reaches every node attached to it.
- Flags: CAMPAIGN_ONLY
- Sources: fandom/Khala, fandom/Amon

#### CMP-02 — Nerazim; Artanis (LotV): Severing the nerve cords [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Permanent disconnection from the Khala was impossible unless the nerve cords were cut. The Nerazim cut theirs and were banished. Zeratul cut Artanis's cord to free him from Amon, at the cost of his own life.
- Counterpart (text): If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out; it is better to enter life maimed.
- Citation: Matt 5:29-30; Mark 9:43-47
- Invariant (interpretation): Freedom from a corrupted channel by cutting the organ that connects you to it, at real cost.
- Residual: Most traditions read Matthew 5:29-30 as hyperbole about the seriousness of sin, not as surgery. The cord itself is not sinful; the channel was hijacked. The cost (loss of communion) matches.
- MAFUBA: 001A: isolation by severing (fail-closed on the channel). The Nerazim, already cut off, were not reachable by Amon through the Khala, which is the argument for isolation before compromise.
- Flags: CAMPAIGN_ONLY
- Sources: fandom/Khala

#### CMP-03 — Keystone (Xel'Naga artifact; WoL): De-infestation of Kerrigan [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): The charged artifact destroys nearby Zerg and at least partially de-infests Kerrigan, restoring her human form. Narud later says de-infestation was not the device's intended use.
- Counterpart (text): The man is found 'clothed and in his right mind'; the boy is left like a corpse, then raised.
- Citation: Mark 5:15; Mark 9:26-27
- Invariant (interpretation): Restoration of the person after removal of the possessing power.
- Residual: The Keystone is a weapon whose de-infesting effect was a side effect, and canon says 'at least partially'. Gospel deliverance is by word and intended. Heart of the Swarm later has Kerrigan re-infested by her own choice, which has no Gospel counterpart.
- Flags: CAMPAIGN_ONLY
- Sources: fandom/Keystone

#### SC2-Z18 — Ultralisk: Frenzied [WEAK]
- Mechanic (game canon): Immune to snares, stuns, mind control (including Neural Parasite) and movement effects.
- Counterpart (text): The evil one does not touch the one born of God.
- Citation: 1 John 5:18
- Invariant (interpretation): Immunity to possession.
- Residual: 1 John 5:18 grounds protection in being 'born of God' (relationship). Frenzied is a trait of the Zerg beast itself, which inverts the text.
- Sources: sc2/Ultralisk (Legacy of the Void)

### Grading rule
STRONG needs three or more shared causal features, a text that itself describes the structure, and survival of the recorded disanalogy. Names borrowed from religious vocabulary earn nothing.
